verdict.rationale: PayPal supports standard OAuth client-credential API keys per app (client ID/secret) and its remote MCP server is OAuth-gated (paypal-probe-4 shows a live 401 challenge with documented authorization server metadata), which lets a developer provision a dedicated app for agent use. But the actual scopes exposed are generic OIDC scopes (openid, email, profile) rather than fine-grained, least-privilege payment/action-level scopes tailored to agent tool use, and no docs describe minting restricted-permission credentials specifically for AI agents (e.g., read-only, spend caps, tool-limited tokens). missing for 10: documented fine-grained/least-privilege scope model for agent credentials, explicit guidance on restricting an agent's app permissions to specific PayPal API products/actions, and independent confirmation that scoped tokens are enforced in practice.
